messages:
oliver (customer): hey team, hitting broken SSE in prod. clients on our webapp sometimes get a partial event stream then connection drops. works fine when i curl the endpoint over http/1.1 locally but the app (http/2) gets truncated messages and reconnect spam.

maria (support): sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the raw request/response you see from the browser and from curl? quick q: are you going through a gRPC gateway or any proxy that might translate h2->h1?

oliver (customer): thanks. we run a grpc-gateway (Envoy in front) that speaks HTTP/2 to clients and translates to HTTP/1.1 to the backend. browser uses native fetch/eventsource. here's a minimal repro curl we used:

```
# simulate http/2 client
curl -v --http2 https://api.example.com/v1/stream?chat_id=abc -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N
```

with that curl i sometimes see full SSE, sometimes: last chunk missing, then connection closes with RST in browser console. curl -v shows: "* Received RST_STREAM with error code 0x1 (PROTOCOL_ERROR)" occasionally.

cheng (eng-runtime): ok this matches a common H2->H1 gateway chunking mismatch. when a gateway converts HTTP/2 DATA frames to HTTP/1.1, it must forward Transfer-Encoding: chunked and flush properly. some gateways buffer until EOF and then send one big chunk -> browsers waiting for event boundary and then RST. can you grab the upstream (backend-facing) request headers from Envoy?

oliver (customer): grabbing now. infra-bot shows a recent deploy at 11:24 (might be related). but here's the upstream request snippet from Envoy access log (redacted):

```
UPSTREAM_HEADERS: :method: GET
:scheme: http
:path: /internal/stream?chat_id=abc
accept: text/event-stream
user-agent: envoy/1.20
x-forwarded-for: 10.0.0.5
```

no Transfer-Encoding header present there. backend (our app) logs show it wrote events with flush() after each write. but no chunked header so backend thinks connection will close to signal body end.

maria (support): that Transfer-Encoding absence is a red flag. some HTTP/1.1 servers expect either Content-Length or chunked. If gateway is stripping Transfer-Encoding but streaming data, clients might see partial frames or get RST when gateway decides to close the stream.

cheng (eng-runtime): two angles to triage: 1) confirm whether Envoy is configured to buffer/aggregate the response; 2) test a path that preserves HTTP/2 to backend (h2 passthrough) to see if problem goes away. quick tests:

- curl with --http2-prior-knowledge directly to backend (bypass gateway) should produce steady SSE.
- curl to gateway with --http2 and add -H "Connection: keep-alive" and -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" to see if gateway honors it.

oliver (customer): tried prior-knowledge to backend: steady stream works. to gateway, adding Transfer-Encoding manually made it marginally better but still flakey. here's a snippet from browser console when stream dies:

```
EventSource failed: Connection to https://api.example.com/v1/stream was interrupted while the page was loading.
```

and server side we sometimes see: `connection reset by peer` and `write failed: broken pipe`.

maria (support): if backend flushes and gateway buffers, gateway might re-chunk on its own but not mark chunk boundaries as SSE expects (newlines/colon prefixes). Also some intermediaries (Cloudflare, CDNs) will disable streaming for responses without specific headers. ask: are there any CDN rules?

oliver (customer): yes we have Cloudflare in front of Envoy (we use Cloudflare Spectrum for TCP passthrough but HTTP is proxied). I can test disabling CF.

cheng (eng-runtime): useful checklist:
- Ensure gateway/proxy uses "proxy_buffering off" or equivalent (NGINX) / disable response buffering in Envoy (set "stream_idle_timeout" and ensure "use_remote_address" not rebuffering).
- Make sure the gateway forwards Transfer-Encoding: chunked and doesn't force Content-Length.
- If using grpc-gateway: switch to streaming gRPC (grpc to grpc) rather than grpc->http1 translation for SSE-like streams. gRPC-Gateway is meant for unary conversions and often buffers responses.
- Look for RST_STREAM codes in the h2 trace: CANCEL vs PROTOCOL_ERROR give different clues. CANCEL often means upstream closed early. PROTOCOL_ERROR means the frames didn't line up.

oliver (customer): i pulled an h2 frame dump via nghttp and saw: final frames before close are: DATA (len 512), RST_STREAM (error=1). no GOAWAY. so looks like PROTOCOL_ERROR from peer.

maria (support): thanks — that suggests the gateway or client detected a protocol violation (maybe unsupported trailers or incorrect window update). Next repro steps for us to debug: can you (1) collect full verbose curl to gateway: `curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N https://...` (attach both curl and backend logs around the timestamp), (2) dump Envoy logs at debug level for that stream, (3) temporarily bypass Cloudflare to rule out CDN buffering.

cheng (eng-runtime): also try this minimal Node fetch SSE client to see if behavior differs from browser EventSource (helps isolate client):

```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/v1/stream?chat_id=abc', {headers: {'Accept': 'text/event-stream'}, decompress: false});
  res.body.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
})();
```

oliver (customer): i ran node-fetch -> it shows the same truncation pattern. so likely gateway+cloudflare combo.

maria (support): concrete mitigation options:
- Configure Envoy to use HTTP/2 between client and backend (h2 passthrough) so there's no translation. Envoy supports http2 to upstream; set `use_http2: true` on cluster config.
- If you must translate to HTTP/1.1, ensure backend sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and gateway disables buffering and sends intermediate flushes. For NGINX: `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection '';`
- For Envoy, ensure `streaming` is enabled and avoid `grpc_json_transcoder` if used for streaming conversions.
- As a fallback, implement a reconnect-safe SSE pattern: include a monotonically increasing event id (id: <n>) and client reconnection logic using Last-Event-ID header so clients can resume without user-visible truncation.

cheng (eng-runtime): additional note: RST_STREAM PROTOCOL_ERROR sometimes happens if an intermediary tries to send Trailers over h2 but backend sent chunked with a trailer name that violates h2 reserved header rules (e.g., using uppercase). Ensure trailers are lowercase and allowed.

oliver (customer): good point — our app emits a "X-Progress: 75" trailer occasionally. looks like it's uppercase. i'll change to lowercase and re-run.

infra-bot: deployment 2026-02-25T11:24:00Z completed to svc/ingress (rev 124).

oliver (customer): changed trailer key to `x-progress` and toggled Envoy to enable upstream http2 for that cluster. reran curl -> stable streaming for 30 minutes with no RST. deploying to prod now to verify.

maria (support): excellent. please keep us posted. if the prod swap still shows sporadic disconnects, next steps: we can pull h2 traces and request an Envoy config dump to check timeouts and buffer settings. also consider adding `retry: 3000` SSE field to help client backoff during transient drops. :thumbsup:

cheng (eng-runtime): logging/action items:
- oliver to attach curl -vv + backend logs for failing windows (if reoccurs).
- oliver to confirm Cloudflare bypass results.
- eng-runtime to prepare a short runbook on h2->h1 streaming pitfalls (we'll include chunked headers, trailers, Envoy settings, and example nginx/edge configs).

oliver (customer): will do. thanks all for the quick help, this was actionable and reproducible.

maria (support): marking thread as follow-up until prod stable. if you want a zoom post-mortem after prod verify we can schedule with eng-runtime.
